transcript.text: Indesit dryer making a horrible squealing noise when it starts up, goes away after a few mins. Still dries fine

A squealing noise that fades after a few minutes is very often caused by the drive belt slipping on a pulley, or a worn idler/jockey wheel that needs to warm up and grip properly. Another possibility is a drum support roller that is stiff when cold but loosens up as it heats. To distinguish between these, please check if the squeal stops once the drum reaches full speed (pointing to belt/tensioner issues) or persists throughout the cycle (suggesting a bearing or roller issue).
It squeals for the first 2-5 minutes of the cycle, then it quietens down. It doesn't happen every cycle, though, and it's worse on cold mornings.

That pattern—squealing only when cold and fading after a few minutes—is classic for a worn idler (jockey) pulley bearing. The grease stiffens in the cold, causing the squeal until friction warms it up; an intermittent belt is also possible but less likely to be so temperature-dependent. To confirm this, please unplug the dryer and turn the drum by hand: if you feel roughness or hear a grind/squeak while rotating it manually, that points directly to the pulley or rollers needing replacement.
Ok, I unplugged it and turned the drum by hand. It turns but there's a slight squeak/scrape and it feels a little rough.

The manual check suggests the issue is mechanical friction in the drum drive area. Given that the squeal happens only when cold and fades as it warms up, this points strongly to a worn idler (jockey) pulley bearing where the grease has stiffened or dried out. A drum support roller could also cause roughness, but the temperature-dependent squealing is classic for the tensioner pulley. This is not something that can be fixed without dismantling the dryer to access the belt and pulleys. As this involves internal components and electrical isolation, I recommend calling a qualified appliance engineer to carry out the repair safely.
